content:
#1 Finitely generated projective modules with an inner product can be seen as an algebraic version of vector bundles with a metric, like the tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold. Have people used this idea to study the more “metric” aspects of Riemannian geometry in an algebraic way?

(I see some references at Hilbert module, are there more?)
subject: Algebraic Riemannian geometry

content:
#2 There is:

  • Jens Kaad: A Serre–Swan theorem for bundles of bounded geometry, Journal of Functional Analysis 265 10 (2013) 2465-2499 [doi;10.1016/j.jfa.2013.06.005]

where an analogue of Serre-Swan for Hilbert bundles is discussed. (But the focus is on the issue of non-compactness of the base manifold and the interest in Hilbert bundles seems to be primarily in their infinite rank, not primarily in their inner product.)

There is also:

  • Danka Lučić, Enrico Pasqualetto: The Serre-Swan theorem for normed modules [arXiv:1803.02911]

but this is concerned with the situation over measure spaces.

On the top of their p. 3 these authors seem to attribute the case of Serre-Swan for Riemannian manifolds to

  • Jet Nestruev: Smooth manifolds and Observables, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 220 Springer (2002, 2020) [doi:10.1007/978-3-030-45650-4, ISBN:0-387-95543-7, pdf]

but (while this author certainly discusses the ordinary Serre-Swan theorem as well as the “smooth Serre-Swan theorem”) I don’t see what particular statement in that book they may have in mind concerning Riemannian geometry (which is barely mentioned there).
subject: Algebraic Riemannian geometry

content:
#3 Thank you!

(About Nestruev’s book: I think they mean Proposition 11.24 and around that.)
